paragraphs: Doorman sells software that keeps student phones from becoming a distraction during class instead of taking the phones away. Schools activate it with hardware tags placed in each room, which students tap with a phone and which double as an attendance record.

Once a phone is tapped in, social media, messaging, notifications and websites are blocked while approved apps stay reachable. Attempts to work around the block are documented so administrators can enforce the policy consistently. The system pulls rosters from a school's student information system and keeps them current as students come and go. Bell schedules can be synced the same way or set by hand, with exceptions for a class or a single student. The company says traffic is encrypted and that it stores no sensitive personal data.

Doorman positions itself against the two alternatives districts usually weigh, arguing that pouches lock learning away along with the phone. It makes a similar case against parental-control apps, which depend on every family installing and configuring settings. The stated ambition reaches past phones to school operations generally, with a goal of helping schools operate ten years ahead.

quote.text: A Distraction-Free Campus, Activated with One Tap.
